To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are five different patterns of the positive point to plane dc corona containing a ripple, which can be clearly identified with respect to other discharge patterns.
the PRPD patterns from positive dc corona driven by half-wave rectified voltages can be classified into five groups that represent the four stages and their transition zones.

the pattern formation of a positive corona driven by an ac voltage is a superposition of patterns of a positive coronadriver by a dc voltage with the same mean voltage and patterns of a negative corona driven by the same ac voltage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the pattern formation in the positive point to plane gap driven by a DC-voltage containing ripple.
the development of a pattern recognition system for the classification of different stages of the positive point to plane discharge.
the identification of the PRPD patterns that can be expected from positive corona driven by dc voltages containing ripple.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PRPD patterns of the positive point-to-plane discharge in air are not only a function of the voltage polarity, but also of the voltage waveform and its frequency.
the pattern formation in the PRPD diagram of corona driven by DC voltage with a ripple is not only dependent on the polarity of the voltage but also on the frequency of the ripple.
the pattern formation is caused by the interaction of the corona discharge with its own electric field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pattern formation of positive dc corona can be described by three different stages, which are separated by transition regions, where patterns from two stages can be found.

the pattern formation of a positive point to plane discharge driven by a dc voltage with ripple can be described by the four stages of the PRPD pattern and that the pattern formation depends on the applied dc voltage and the discharge current.

the PRPD pattern for a positive point to plane dc corona driven by an AC voltage containing a ripple is a function of the applied voltage, which is determined by the voltage level and the voltage ripple.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pattern formation in positive corona can be explained in a similar way as in the case of other dc discharge sources, i.e. the pattern formation in dc discharge sources can be explained in terms of the underlying physical processes, which are the same for all of them.
the PRPD pattern of positive corona is not a unique fingerprint of the corona process but depends on the applied voltage and the measurement setup.
the patterns can be used as a tool for the assessment of the corona onset and breakdown streamer formation.
